methodology.intro: Every PS2 subsystem and every significant part of Zmbor, with a status written by hand and checked by `tools/status/validate_dashboard.py` against the evidence it cites. The two diagrams are generated from `docs/status/components.json` by `tools/status/generate_dashboard.py`. A component's colour says how far its behaviour is known to be correct, not how much code exists.
rules: Hardware evidence means a ps2autotests program whose output matches the `.expected` file printed by a real PS2, a unit test whose expected values are real-PS2 results (`hwvec`), or a formal proof (Z3). Unit tests written from documentation, PCSX2 or the GS manual are tests, not hardware evidence.

A hardware component is `VERIFIED_COMPLETE` only if its scope is enumerated in a form the validator checks (an instruction list against the hardware-confirmed set, or a proof) and every item is covered by a matching hardware program, with no mismatching program touching it. One passing program without an enumerated scope gives `VERIFIED_PARTIAL`.
A framework component (recompiler, tools) is `VERIFIED_COMPLETE` when its stated scope is fully covered by tests or proofs that run in CI.

HLE components (`implementation: hle`) replace a library or IOP module at call level. They are `HLE_OR_STUB` unless hardware programs exercise them, in which case they are `VERIFIED_PARTIAL`, never complete.

Group and section states are not stored: they are the counts of their components. Passing tests never upgrade a status automatically; a status change is an edit of components.json with matching evidence.

Percentages appear only where a numerator and a denominator are enumerated: ps2autotests output lines and programs, and hardware-confirmed instructions per decoded instruction class. Each is truncated, never rounded up.
`NOT_APPLICABLE` entries are scope proposals that the owner must confirm; `UNKNOWN` means no measurement exists.

statuses.VERIFIED_COMPLETE: defined scope fully implemented and independently verified (rules above)
statuses.VERIFIED_PARTIAL: some behaviour verified, relevant gaps remain
statuses.IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED: implementation exists without sufficient correctness evidence
statuses.HLE_OR_STUB: approximate or placeholder behaviour (high-level emulation or stub)
statuses.MISSING: required feature has no functional implementation
statuses.NOT_APPLICABLE: deliberately outside the declared scope (proposed; owner confirms)

hardware_source.description: the hardware matrix of the acceptance gate run on c7e5960 (p7_gate4); main a13b47a (merge of PR #5) has the identical tree b79613e.

isa_coverage.method: Instruction coverage: the denominator is every mnemonic the recompiler's decode tables name for a class (`ps2xRecomp/include/ps2recomp/instructions.h`; it includes MIPS encodings the EE does not implement, which can only lower the value). An instruction counts as hardware-confirmed when a ps2autotests program that matches real-PS2 output exactly names it in its output and no mismatching program does. Instructions a program executes without naming them (for example SYNC) are not counted. VU micro-mode and COP0 programs do not name instructions, so those classes are not measured.
